title: Robert Fagel (The Hague) to Prince William V, 18 June 1804 (KHA A31 PWV inv. 337; DECODE R2238)

steps.what: Fetched DECODE R2238 record and its three page images with the session cookie; page 3 carries the cipher, pages 2 and 1 are clear.
Transcribed the cipher passage (128 groups, one interlinear insertion) and the clear context.
Grand Chiffre du Stadhouder (R1024, 1782) via the DECODE key transcription, direct lookup.
Grand Chiffre with the additive Tableau (11 rows x 17 values) from every row and column start, scored on syllable fit of dot-joined groups.
R2240 Orange key (letters 1-100, names 100-6006); R1035 and R1891 Dutch codebooks; siblings R2236, R2237, R2239 in the same inventory number.
Fagel family key sets NA 1.10.29 inv. 1257-1267 (DECODE R2842-R2852), one interior page each: all Dutch-vocabulary codes.
Grand Chiffre R1024 with every constant offset -2600..+2600, scored on syllable fit: best offsets give nonsense.

Swept all 6,396 DECODE key records for keys dated 1790-1815 (149) and French-language keys from 1780 (30): apart from those already tested, none is Dutch or Orange; the BL Add MS 32257/32264/32292 French keys are intercepted French government ciphers. Web search found no printed decipherment and no KHA cipher key online.

Queried the current KHA A31 online inventory. DECODE's old inv. nr. 337 no longer corresponds to the modern catalogue. The target belongs contextually in A31-2306-2308 (Batavian compensation negotiations, 1802-1804), especially files 2307/2308; adjacent A31-2292-2293 includes Fagel, D'Yvoy, Van Olden and a catalogue note on fl. 500,000 for the French.

Contemporary sources identify the negotiation, the opposing plenipotentiaries, the proposed five-million-guilder settlement, and Fagel and D'Yvoy's short German journey immediately after the letter. This strongly constrains the subject but does not uniquely determine the 128 code groups.

Checked DECODE transcription views and searched Robert Fagel correspondence while logged in. R2238 and R2236 have no contributed transcription; R2237 is decrypted but uses a visibly different small-number system. No other Robert Fagel correspondence record supplies a parallel text.

Inspected BL Add MS 32264 candidates R8963/R8964 (French Cypher 1798-1799), R8984 (1805), and adjacent records R8965-R8983. Their ranges are about 1-750 or 1-250, or they are short correspondence specimens; none matches the verified four-digit groups 1531, 1731, and 2510.
Checked the current Nationaal Archief catalogue for Fagel 1.10.29 inv. nr. 1909. The relevant Robert Fagel series is marked PHYSICAL and exposes no digital object or IIIF scan.

Searched the complete OCR of Colenbrander, Gedenkstukken IV (1908), including documents 790-804 and 813. The 18 June 1804 letter is not printed, but the edition confirms the exact compensation/bribery context and prints later Robert Fagel reports from Paris.

The current Royal Collections catalogue identifies KHA A31-902, a separate one-packet file of papers concerning ciphers used at court, broadly dated to the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries. It has no online scans and is the strongest physical target for the missing 1804 key.

outcome.method_basis: The 128 code groups on DECODE R2238 were transcribed, and every candidate Orange, Fagel and DECODE key of 1780-1815 (the Grand Chiffre R1024 with its tableau and renumberings, R2240, R1035, R1891, R2842-R2852) was ruled out; no key or clear copy was located.
outcome.notes: Key not located. The code (about 2500 groups) is too large for 128 groups of text to yield a unique exact reading without the key. Best physical target: KHA A31-902 (court cipher papers), followed by A31-2307/2308 (and A31-2292/2293) plus NA 1.10.29 no. 1909, asking for the codebook or a duplicate/deciphered copy of the 18 June 1804 letter.

prior.where: DECODE status non-decrypted; no decipherment on the letter

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.
